one_liner: Single-purpose Rust HTTPS server that returns the caller's IP; one first-party wrk run beat a one-worker nginx 1.49x.
what_it_does: A command-line server that accepts HTTPS connections (HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 via ALPN, or HTTP/2 only with -2) and answers every request, whatever its path or method, with the client's IP address as a plain-text body. It backs the author's ip.erix.dev:11313 endpoint for the wut CLI. It is a binary, not a library; the only configuration is bind addresses, certificate and key paths, a log interval and the HTTP/2-only flag.
how_it_is_fast: There is no special technique: it is about 290 lines on hyper 0.14 + tokio 1.35 with rustls 0.21 (ring) for TLS, built with LTO, codegen-units = 1 and strip. The IP string is formatted once per connection in make_service_fn and cloned into each response, so a keep-alive connection only clones a short string per request, and hyper's response carries only date and content-length headers (about 90 bytes per response against nginx's 114, derived from page data). Any throughput gap against nginx comes from different TLS stacks and runtimes, not from a language effect.
when_to_use: You need a self-hosted 'what is my IP' endpoint over HTTPS and want a tiny binary instead of an nginx config.
Clients connect directly (no reverse proxy or load balancer in front), because the answer is the TCP peer address.
As a minimal hyper 0.14 + rustls example of a TLS server with ALPN for HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2.
when_not_to_use: Anything beyond echoing the client IP: no routing, static files, headers, proxying or configuration file.
Behind a proxy, CDN or load balancer: there is no X-Forwarded-For or PROXY-protocol support, so it reports the proxy's address.
Where you need current, patched dependencies: the lockfile pins h2 0.3.24, hyper 0.14 and rustls 0.21, and the project has been idle since March 2024.
Deployments that renew certificates without restarts: certificates are read once at startup and hot reload is only listed as planned.
Windows: shutdown handling uses tokio::signal::unix, so it builds only on Unix.

integration.form: binary (Cargo project; not published on crates.io)
integration.dependencies: hyper 0.14.28, hyper-rustls 0.24.2, rustls 0.21.10 (ring 0.17), tokio 1.35.1, tokio-rustls 0.24.1, h2 0.3.24, clap 4.4, anyhow, env_logger, log, rustls-pemfile 1, futures-util
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 2021 edition; exact MSRV not documented
integration.thread_safety: tokio multi-thread runtime via #[tokio::main]; per-connection state only, plus one shared atomic counter
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: replaces only an nginx server block of the form 'return 200 "$remote_addr"'; nothing else nginx does

gotchas: Harness inconsistency (derived from page data): the wut-server wrk output reports 38,110.60 req/s at 45.00 ms average latency, which by Little's law needs about 1,715 requests in flight, but wrk with 6 threads and 1000 connections opens 996 connections with one request each, capping throughput near 22,100 req/s at that latency. The nginx run is consistent (about 720 in flight). So the wut-server output was not a plain single-request-per-connection wrk run as printed (an unshown pipelining script, or output from different runs); the wrk command line and any script are not published.

The server's own 'Requests per second' log counts connections, not requests (the counter is incremented in make_service_fn, once per connection), and start_counter stores the interval delta in prev_elapsed_time instead of the cumulative time, so per-interval rates are wrong after the second interval; the server log cannot cross-check the wrk numbers.

Cargo.lock pins h2 0.3.24, inside RUSTSEC-2024-0332 (CONTINUATION frame flood, patched in 0.3.26), and HTTP/2 is enabled by default through with_all_versions_alpn; rustls 0.21.10 is inside RUSTSEC-2024-0336's range, though that advisory says the tokio-rustls path is not affected. Run cargo update before deploying.
Default bind is 127.0.0.1:11313 and [::1]:11313, so it is unreachable from outside until -b is set; the private key file must hold exactly one key (EC, PKCS#8 or RSA) or startup fails.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it only when the job is literally 'return the client IP over TLS'; for a general static-response server that beats nginx, statico (Rust, tokio or monoio, measured against nginx 'return' at 1 and 4 threads) or routez (fixed and TLS responses against nginx and HAProxy) have broader evidence, and the HttpArena tokio entry is the better-measured raw-tokio data point.
verified_claims_summary: One first-party wrk run per server (10 s, 6 threads, 1000 connections, HTTPS with HTTP/1.1) from a Ryzen 5600 client over the internet to a single-core EPYC 7302P server: wut-server 38,110.60 req/s against nginx with one worker, LTO and static OpenSSL at 25,650.31 req/s (1.49x, derived from page data), with nginx logging 95 connect and 17 read errors; versions, compiler flags and the wrk command are not given, and the wut-server output is internally inconsistent (see gotchas).
status_note: Stale since 2024-03-09 (2 commits, the second a README typo fix; 0 stars; no issues; not on crates.io) but MIT-licensed and small enough to copy, with superseded hyper 0.14 and rustls 0.21 dependencies that need upgrading; the speed claim should be treated as unreliable because the published wrk output fails a Little's-law check.
